title: Notes on the Locality and Population of the Tribes on the North-Eastern Frontier of India: Tangkhul and Luhuppa Wordlist
creator: G. H. Damant
publisher: Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland, London
notes: Important late 19th-century administrative wordlist comparing Tangkhul terms before missionary contact published in JRAS. Out of copyright.
background: Compiled by British frontier administrator G. H. Damant and published posthumously in the Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society of Great Britain and Ireland (New Series, Vol. 12, No. 2, 1880). Presents demographic surveys, geographic boundaries, and comparative vocabularies for hill tribes including the Tangkhul (Luhuppa). Provides crucial late 19th-century lexical data collected before the introduction of mission schools and the Roman literary standard.
phonology_notes: Demonstrates 19th-century phonetic orthography and records customary institutional terms relating to cattle sacrifice, chieftainship, and mountain topography.

entries.example: Iram khamatha (Our village is honorable and good).
Kaphung zanshor (Slopes of the mountain range).
Se kakhayei (Gifting mithun during feast negotiations).
Sha kakhang (Hunting wild quarry in the high forest).
Hui eina sha khangavai (Pursuing mountain game with hound).
Zingsho kashok (Sunrise breaking over the hills).
Sirak ngalong (Stars shining in the clear night).
Haora kakhon (Draping the prestigious warrior shawl).
Hangvana shiyan kakazip (The elders assembling to adjudicate laws).
